# Prior-art search, pass 2: LLMs and agents on fire tasks, 2025-2026 only

THE PROJECT'S ANGLE, FIXED. How large language models and AI agents perform across many kinds of fire
tasks: what has been found, what insights follow, and where the field should go. The work will have a
survey component (what is already known about LLMs and agents on fire tasks) and a benchmark component
(evaluating LLMs and agents across those tasks).

YOUR JOB. Find existing work from 2025-01-01 through 2026-09-13 that bears on that angle, and record
what each work found. Two uses: (1) checking whether anyone has already surveyed and benchmarked LLMs
and agents across fire tasks, and (2) collecting the findings the survey component will organize.
Do not design anything and do not recommend what to build.

IN SCOPE. LLMs, vision-language models, multimodal LLMs, and LLM-based agents or multi-agent systems,
applied to wildfire, structure fire, fire science, fire engineering, fire operations, or fire-related
emergency management. Also broader disaster or Earth-science LLM/agent work that includes at least one
fire task. Non-LLM fire AI (CNNs, spread models, classic ML) is out of scope unless it compares against
LLMs or agents.

RULES.
- Date window: first public version (arXiv v1, preprint, or publication) between 2025-01-01 and
  2026-09-13. Record the date you saw.
- Include a work only after fetching a page that confirms it: arXiv abstract page, DOI landing page,
  venue or proceedings page, OpenReview page, or the project's GitHub repository. Record that URL.
  Seen only in a search snippet means verified_by_fetch false.
- Never invent authors, dates, venues, model names, or numbers. Write "unknown" when not confirmed.
- Stay inside your own angle; other units cover the rest. Aim for 10 to 25 works.

TASK CATEGORIES. Tag each work with every category it evaluates:
  knowledge-qa                 fire science, engineering, codes, or safety question answering
  document-understanding       incident reports, after-action reviews, records, extraction
  detection-perception         fire or smoke recognition from imagery or video by VLMs or MLLMs
  forecasting-prediction       spread, risk, danger, occurrence, or behavior prediction by LLMs or agents
  geospatial-analysis          GIS reasoning, spatial computation, map or remote-sensing interpretation
  decision-support-operations  resource allocation, dispatch, evacuation, incident command
  simulation-coupled-agents    agents that drive or interpret fire simulators
  communication-alerts         public warnings, crisis communication, social media analysis
  data-retrieval-tools         agents that query fire databases, APIs, or tools
  other                        say what

CLOSENESS TO THE PROJECT (0 to 3).
  3  surveys LLM/agent work on fire tasks broadly AND evaluates LLMs or agents across many fire tasks
  2  does one half well and the other partially
  1  evaluates LLMs or agents on one or two fire task categories, or surveys LLMs in disasters with fire
     as a minor part
  0  adjacent: LLM or agent work in disaster or Earth science with no fire task

# Verification of prior-art records (prun, Agy)

Each record below was written by an earlier search worker, who may have misread a page or filled a gap
from memory. Your job is to check each record against its source, one by one. Do not search for new
works.

For each record:
1. Fetch the URL. If it fails or points to the wrong work, search for the exact title and fetch the
   work's own page (arXiv abstract page, DOI landing page, publisher page, OpenReview, or official
   report page). When an arXiv abstract page exists, also fetch the arXiv HTML or PDF full text
   when the record's numbers are not in the abstract.
2. Check: the work exists with this title; first author; date of first public version; venue.
3. Check every specific claim in key_finding, models_evaluated, and n_models, especially numbers.
   A claim is "confirmed" only if you saw it on a fetched page. Do not rely on memory.
4. Decide whether the work evaluates LLMs, vision-language models, multimodal LLMs, or LLM-based
   agents (llm_in_scope true) or only non-LLM methods such as RL policies, CNNs, or Earth-observation
   foundation models (llm_in_scope false).
5. Decide whether the work includes at least one fire task (fire_task true or false).

Run every command in the foreground and wait for it to finish. Do not launch background tasks and do
not wait for notifications; nothing will notify you. Write the JSON file before ending your turn, even
